document_name: Code compliant school buildings boost student achievement
llm_reasoning: The study evaluates student achievement after moving to a new school building compliant with building requirements. Its stated outcome is FCAT mathematics and reading scores, and the context does not identify a climate-mitigation aim or assess emissions, energy use, or another listed mitigation outcome. Although the study uses a causal-comparative design, the substantive climate-mitigation criterion is not met.
llm_verbatim_text: the research question for the inquiry was whether the percentage of students passing the FCAT mathematics and reading subtests increases after transitioning from an old school building into a new 2000 UBC (Uniform Building Code) compliant facility.
